overall: Atlanta has already peaked for the day with a running max of 91.4°F reached by 15:00 ET, holding flat through 18:34 ET — nearly 3.5 hours without a new high. The current temperature of 89.6°F is already 1.8°F below that peak, and with zero velocity and well past peak solar heating for a June afternoon, the day is effectively thermally done. Conditions are humid (dewpoint 69.8°F) but no late-day convective surge appears to be underway.
forecast_obs_notes: Three of the four models (GFS 91.3°F, HRRR 91.3°F, ECMWF 89.7°F) have already been equaled or surpassed by the observed running max of 91.4°F, confirming the day ran near the warmer end of guidance. Only NBM at 92.3°F remains unverified and would require a ~+0.9°F surge from here, which is inconsistent with the current cooling trend and the flat velocity signal.
max_temp_prediction: The daily high is almost certainly locked in at 91.4°F. With temperatures declining, zero warming velocity at 18:34 ET, and no model signal suggesting a late-day resurgence, the probability of exceeding the current running max is very low. Confidence is high that 91.4°F is the final TMAX, with only a marginal chance of a trivial tick higher (e.g., 91.5°F) if there is any brief residual surface heating.
